articles.title: Solheim Cup: Anna Nordqvist named as Team Europe's captain for 2026 contest against Team USA in the Netherlands
articles.summary: Anna Nordqvist succeeds Suzann Pettersen as Solheim Cup captain and will lead Team Europe for the 2026 contest in the Netherlands; Nordqvist has played in nine consecutive Solheim Cups; Team USA are defending champions after their 2024 win
articles.body:
Nordqvist has featured in each of the last nine Solheim Cups as a player - an ever-present member of the European side since her 2009 debut - with the Swede part of four winning European teams and another that retained the trophy with a tie.

The three-time major champion was a playing vice-captain for Pettersen during the last two editions, where Europe retained the trophy with a historic 14-14 tie in Spain in 2023 before losing to the United States a year later.

Nordqvist now succeeds Pettersen as captain for the next edition of the biennial contest, held at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands from September 11-13, 2026, where Europe will look to regain the trophy and claim a first victory in five years.

"I am so honoured to be appointed as the 2026 European Solheim Cup captain," Nordqvist said. "Whether we were winning or losing, the Solheim Cup has played such a huge part in my career ever since I made my debut in 2009 in Chicago.

"The friendships I have made, and the memories created during the nine matches I've played, make it so incredibly special to be given the opportunity to be European captain at my 10th Solheim Cup!"

Nordqvist has won six additional LPGA Tour titles and four Ladies European Tour titles alongside her major wins, including the 2022 Dutch Ladies Open, with the 37-year-old planning to keep playing long beyond the 2026 Solheim Cup.

Team USA have yet to announce their next Solheim Cup captain, with Stacy Lewis holding the role for the past two editions. Angela Stanford and Morgan Pressel, vice-captains for the last two contests, are other potential contenders.

New captain Nordqvist's past Solheim success

Nordqvist is tied-second in most Solheim Cup appearances for Team Europe, with former captains Pettersen and Catriona Matthew also within three of Dame Laura Davies' record of 12.

She won two points from four matches during each of her first two appearances, including in Europe's dramatic 15-13 victory in 2011 that ended a run of three consecutive Team USA successes.

Nordqvist fired the first hole-in-one in Solheim Cup history during Europe's record-breaking 2013 victory, then was one of only three European players to win their singles matches on the final day of USA's historic comeback in 2015.

The Solheim Cup stalwart finished as Europe's top-scorer during their 2017 defeat, winning 3.5 points from her four matches, with Nordqvist defeating Pressel on the last day of Europe's historic 14.5-13.5 at Gleneagles two years later.

She partnered rookie Matilda Castren to two wins during Europe's successful title defence on American soil in 2021, before contributing a final-day point in the historic draw in 2023 and earning two points for Europe in last year's 15.5-12.5 loss.

Nordqvist has won 18.5 points from her 35 matches, making her Europe's fifth-highest all-time points scorer behind Davies (25), Annika Sorenstam (24), Matthew (22) and Pettersen (21).

Alexandra Armas, chief executive of the Ladies European Tour, said: "She has been such an important member of the European team over the years - both on and off the course - and she was excellent in the role of playing vice-captain last year.

"She has been a wonderful ambassador for European golf throughout her career, both as an individual and as part of the team. I can tell you that the news of this appointment will no doubt be extremely popular amongst the players."

articles.title: Anna Nordqvist: Team Europe's Solheim Cup captain bids emotional farewell to playing career at LPGA Tour's FM Championship
articles.summary: Anna Nordqvist's playing career ended at the FM Championship on Sunday, 12 days before she captains Team Europe at the Solheim Cup; Ruoning Yin of China ended a two-year wait for a win on the LPGA Tour; watch the Solheim Cup live on Sky Sports Golf from September 11-13
articles.body:
The 39-year-old, who announced this week that Boston would be her farewell, finished on the ninth green at TPC Boston surrounded by fellow players and caddies, signing off with a level-par final round to finish one under for the week.

Her career ends with 16 victories, including three majors, 19 top-10 finishes in major championships and five Solheim Cup triumphs from nine consecutive appearances. Across 18 years, she has built a body of work that ranks among the finest of any European golfer of her generation.

LPGA Hall of Famer Pat Bradley embraced her and playing partner Ariya Jutanugarn had already reduced her to tears at the very first hole by telling her how happy she was to share the legendary Swede's final round.

"Nothing ever prepares you for this moment. I'm definitely going to miss it," Nordqvist said. "Part of me feels like I still have so much more left in me but I'm just forever grateful for everything this game and the LPGA family has done for me.

"I came out on tour in 2009 as a 21-year-old with no family in the US, and everyone has been just such a huge support."

Asked about her legacy, she said: "So many people think your career is a straight line upwards. I feel like I've gone through a lot of ups and downs both on and off the course. What I want to be remembered for is the fact that I never gave up.

"I thought about quitting in 2012, 2013. I was really, really close to walking away. If my younger brother hadn't come out and caddied for me that summer, I don't think I would be sitting here. So he saved my career."

The Swede won the first of her three majors as a rookie in 2009 and added the Evian Championship in 2017, but it is the 2021 AIG Women's Open at Carnoustie she holds dearest.

"It's still one of those moments I pinch myself," she said. "Did this really happen? No one can ever take that away from me, and it's definitely the most proud moment of my career."

Her nine consecutive Solheim Cup appearances yielded five European victories and, after serving as a playing vice-captain in the last two editions, she now turns her full attention to the captaincy - a role she says has consumed her for the past 18 months.

"All the work you put in, you put in for others to prepare for that one week," she said. "The satisfaction of seeing your hard work pay off won't be until the actual Solheim Cup.

"Hopefully the players are going to see all the hard work that me and the rest of the background team have put in, because it really takes a village to make an event like that happen."

Family sits at the heart of both the decision and what comes next, Nordqvist admitting she has "missed so many birthdays" across two decades of sacrifice. Her nieces and nephews will be waiting in the Netherlands in two weeks, where Bernardus Golf hosts the first assignment of the next chapter of her life.

The gifts had begun before the goodbye even started.

Former world No 1 Lydia Ko presented her with a bottle earlier in the week, and Nordqvist admitted she had needed a moment to identify what it was.

"A really nice bottle of, I think it was champagne, maybe, I'm not sure. I don't drink a ton."

The vintage actually turned out to be 2009, the year her rookie season began – a fitting touch.

A second bottle of the same label was waiting as she came off the course on Sunday. This one was a 2017, the year she won the Evian Championship, her first major on European soil.

There had been tears all day, but she left the interview room smiling.

"So 2017 was a memorable one," she said. "My mascara is obviously waterproof, so that's a good sign."

Ruoning Yin of China claimed the title in the end with a two-stroke victory over Hyo Joo Kim, the 23-year-old closing with a two-under 70 crowned by a birdie at the last.

It ended a 672-day wait for a win stretching back to the 2024 Maybank Championship and involved a key piece of decision making down the stretch.

Yin had drawn level with a 25-foot birdie putt at the par-five 12th and then parred her way through the breeze until the closing par-five, where, with Kim in a bunker, she overruled caddie David Jones' suggestion to play safe.

"David told me to aim a little left and I was just like, let's just go for the green, go for the pin," said the winner. "I hit a good shot and I was telling myself, just slow down and make a good tempo, and then I did it."

The win was the sixth of Yin's career and, allied to her 2023 KPMG Women's PGA Championship, makes her just the sixth player in the last 15 years to collect six LPGA Tour titles including a major before turning 24 – the first since Nelly Korda, while she becomes a second successive Chinese winner of this event after Miranda Wang's 2025 triumph.

Kim's challenge unravelled with a three-putt bogey at the 16th, while Sei Young Kim dropped four shots in three holes after leading with a chip-in at the 11th and had to settle for a share of fourth alongside Rose Zhang, behind Allisen Corpuz who finished third.

World No 1 Korda finished tied-50th in her final outing before the Solheim Cup, while English pair Charley Hull and Lottie Woad finished in a tie for 18th and 27th respectively.

The LPGA Tour and Ladies European Tour both have a week off ahead of the 20th edition of the Solheim Cup, held at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands, where Team Europe look to regain the trophy from Team USA.

articles.title: Flooding causes disruption to West Midlands road and rail travel
articles.summary: Heavy rain floods Hall Green, causing disruption on the line between Moor Street and Stratford.
articles.body:
Storms across the West Midlands have led to more travel disruption.

Heavy rain flooded Hall Green station, causing disruption on the line between Kidderminster/Birmingham Moor Street and Whitlocks End/Stratford-upon-Avon. Passengers were able to use their tickets on bus services, West Midlands Railway said.

A flood warning for the Spadesbourne Brook in Bromsgrove was issued and the Met Office said a yellow warning for heavy rain and thunderstorms was in place. Police issued notices for drivers to be careful if out in the rain saying there was a lot of surface water.

The disruption follows a few days of heavy rain in the region.

Earlier this week, 55 homes in the Perry Barr area experienced internal flooding, with flooding also occurring in Stafford and Burntwood.

A flood warning on the River Stour in Worcestershire has been downgraded to an alert.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler wins FedEx Cup, passes Tiger Woods on all-time money list
articles.summary: Scheffler caps his season with a $10 million paycheck.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — There are moments in golf when you just know something special is happening, when the combination of moment and shot and gallery and course combine to produce magic. On the 211-yard par-3 seconnd hole at East Lake Golf Club, in the final round of the Tour Championship Sunday, Scottie Scheffler stepped up to the tee and did this:

That set an immediate tone for Scheffler as he tried to chase down Viktor Hovland — Scheffler started the day trailing by three — and cap the season off with a third victory in 2026. By hole four, Scheffler had caught him, and by the time he walked off the 18th green, having done what has made him the No. 1 player in the world — dialing things up when the pressure is at its highest — he was three shots clear of the field, and on his way to another massive payday.

On a day at East Lake when birdies were finally hard to come by, Scheffler came home with a 4-under 66, tied for the low round of the day. Behind him, Hovland came home with a 2-over 72.

With the three-shot victory, Scheffler now stands as the FedEx Cup champion and, on a broader scale, the leading money winner in PGA Tour history.

Scheffler officially passed Tiger Woods for that title on Sunday. With a $10 million paycheck Sunday, Scheffler is now at $130,390,661 to Tiger's $120,999,166.

Although Scheffler has enjoyed much larger purses than Woods did in his prime, the overall trend is accurate. Scheffler is now competing against more than his fellow players, he's competing against previous generations.

In theory, the Tour Championship should stand as the crowning event of the PGA Tour's season, the culmination of eight months' worth of competition all over the country (with the occasional detour to Canada and the United Kingdom). In practice, the Tour Championship has struggled to find its identity as both a concept and a tournament. Formats come and go, motivations wax and wane, but through it all, the destination was always the same: East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, home course of Bobby Jones.

Not for much longer, though. In one of two major off-course stories that overshadowed whatever would happen inside the ropes, the PGA Tour announced on Tuesday that East Lake's tenure as the home of the Tour Championship ends after next year. Starting in 2028, the PGA Tour will roll out a new playoff format heavily weighted toward match play — the final two events of the season will be match-play events, with fields narrowing from 32 to 16 to 1. It's a much-needed way to juice the creaky playoff format, but it will cost East Lake its spot at the end of the season's schedule.

On Sunday, as with most every non-Tiger-Woods day at the Tour Championship, the gallery was enthusiastic if not necessarily deeply engaged. Copious merch and hospitality tents line the course, and until late Sunday afternoon, galleries rarely gather more than one deep around any hole. Plus, from a historical perspective, the 30-man Tour Championship, while lucrative, doesn't quite carry the weight of a full-field major.

All these factors combine to make the Tour Championship less of a must-see golf event and more of a lovely place to hang out while golf goes on nearby. The abundant food and drink options, sponsor giveaways and general chill vibe are designed to appeal to the changing sensibilities of modern golf fans, which is usually — though definitely not always — a good idea.

Which leads to the second major non-golf story that sucked up the oxygen at East Lake this week: the reputational self-destruction of Good Good Golf . The YouTube golf lifestyle brand released, and quickly pulled, a controversial ad in partnership with Callaway last Friday, and then spent the next few days attempting to stem the PR damage. But by Thursday, the brand wound had festered; Callaway cut ties with Good Good, and soon afterward, Good Good withdrew from its planned sponsorship of a PGA Tour event. The Tour did not exactly express regret at the brand's departure.

Combined, the off-course action vacuumed up the majority of the golf coverage throughout the tournament's first few days. On the course, though, players took advantage of the wide fairways and enormous greens at East Lake to post some borderline-ridiculous scores. The three last-place finishers on Thursday stood at even par, and only Gary Woodland at +2 finished the week over par.

Nearly a quarter of the field — Scheffler, Hovland, Chris Gotterup, Min Woo Lee, Ryan Gerard, Collin Morikawa and Cameron Young — finished at least one round within two strokes of the lead.

No one quite ran away from the field at East Lake on Sunday, but no one outside of Scheffler could keep the pace set through the first three rounds.

Starting three strokes back of Hovland, Scheffler quickly carved into the lead with that near-ace on the second hole. Another birdie at No. 4 put him into a tie for the lead. Nine holes later, a birdie on the 13th gave Scheffler solo possession of the lead, and even a bogey on the next hole didn't harm him, as Hovland bogeyed the 13th behind him.

Ultimately, the difference came down to the back nine, where Scheffler was 2-under, while Hovland was over 2-over par. And that's what decided it.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler se lleva la FedEx Cup y desbanca a Tiger Woods
articles.standfirst: El número 1 del mundo gana The Tour Championship, su vigésimoquinto torneo en cinco temporadas, y acumula más de 130 millones en premios
articles.summary: El número 1 del mundo gana The Tour Championship, su vigésimoquinto torneo en menos de cuatro temporadas, y acumula más de 130 millones en premios
articles.body: El golf mundial, por encima de cualquier otra lucha, es Scottie Scheffler, el golfista que en Atlanta ganó su segunda FedEX Cup al imponerse en The Tour Championship, la primera en el formato de torneo final único, sin importar ningún tipo de resultado que se arrastrara anteriormente. La victoria certifica muchas cosas. En primer lugar que por cuarta temporada en los cinco últimos años -salvo el 2023 de Jon Rahm-, el texano de 30 años es el mejor golfista del planeta. Definitivamente ya es un golfista de época. En tiempos donde el golf anda dividido y sin una personalidad arrolladora, aunque sí un carisma ganado por autenticidad, Scheffler es uno de los mejores deportistas del planeta sin duda. Domina la clasificación mundial de tal forma que saca casi los mismos puntos a Rory McIlroy, el número 2 mundial, que el norilandés saca al 5.016, el que cierra el ránking. Además, esta victoria en el East Golf Lake, 10 millones de dólares, le supone derrocar a Tiger Woods al frente de las listas de ganancias del PGA Tour, un alzamiento de un simbolismo fabuloso. Scheffler ha ganado en apenas siete cursos en el PGA Tour, 130,39 millones de dólares en su carrera, más de nueve millones que la megaestrella, que desde 2000 lleva liderando esta tabla. (Resultados) El nuevo héroe suma veinticinco títulos desde febrero de 2022, incluido cuatro grandes, cuatro torneos de los playoffs de la FedEx Cup, el oro olímpico, dos The Players. Un palmarés de jubilado con una década como mínimo de gran rendimiento por delante. Ya está entre los 30 golfistas de la historia con más títulos en el PGA Tour. Scheffler juega como un autómata. Como hace especialmente los domingos. Es la razón por la que este año, que parecía regular hasta el Fede St Jud Classic -sólo una victoria en el American Express-, es en términos globales formidable. Ha hecho cinco segundos puestos y tres terceros. En la mitad de los torneos que ha jugado, en total 20, ha quedado en el podio. Números de fuera de serie. En Atlanta, el mandamás del golf cogió la cabeza en solitario en el hoyo 13 de la ronda final por primera vez en todo el torneo. Provocó una carga final fantástica, con golpes como el del 2, un par 3 de 191 metros en la que pone el golpe de salida a 2 dedos del hoyo. Devoró la diferencia de tres golpes con la que había salido a Viktor Hovland, el noruego que soñaba con repetir el éxito de 2023 y dedicársela al fallecido monarca Harald V, pero se desesperó con el putt -dos tiros para birdie tocaron hoyo- y dilapidó su renta frente al empuje de Scheffler. El estadounidense, con una tarjeta de 66 como el sábado, salió de nuevo vencedor. Aún más si cabe. El campeón del carisma sutil.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler Passes Tiger Woods on PGA Tour's Career Earnings List, Rory McIlroy Nears 2nd
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler is well on his way to being one of the best golfers in PGA Tour history, and he surpassed a legend on the career earnings list on Sunday.
articles.body:
Scottie Scheffler is well on his way to being one of the best golfers in PGA Tour history, and he surpassed a legend on the career earnings list on Sunday.

After winning the TOUR Championship, he took over first place on the PGA Tour career earnings list with $130,390,661. Tiger Woods previously led the list with $120,999,166.

Rory McIlroy, who came into this week's tournament with $117,848,372 in career earnings, is also nearing Woods after finishing tied for fourth on Sunday.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler Surges Past Hovland to Win TOUR Championship and FedEx Cup, Full Leaderboard
articles.summary: For the second time in the last three weeks, Scottie Scheffler secured a victory on the PGA Tour.
articles.body:
For the second time in the last three weeks, Scottie Scheffler secured a victory on the PGA Tour.

After winning the FedEx St. Jude Championship earlier this month, Scheffler won the TOUR Championship following a phenomenal final round on Sunday. He surged past Viktor Hovland and finished 16-under par.

The win also secured the FedEx Cup for Scheffler.

Hovland came into Sunday's final round leading the pack but struggled throughout the day, carding three bogeys with just one birdie. That opened the door for Scheffler to pass him, and he made the most of the opportunity.

Scheffler picked up three birdies on the front nine before adding three more on the back nine. He had two bogeys, but his outstanding play otherwise helped him secure the victory by two shots.

Ryan Gerard was also in the mix coming into the final round, but a lousy start quickly hurt his chances. He had a double bogey on the first hole and managed just one birdie on the day to finish third.

Both Gerard and Hovland finished two-over par 70 on Sunday, making things much easier for Scheffler down the stretch.

Scheffler had a great start to the season when he won The American Express in January, but unlike last season, he didn't stack up wins with ease. Until his performance at the FedEx St. Jude Championship, he hadn't won an event, though he finished near the top of the leaderboard in countless tournaments.

He battled through hand, foot and mouth disease at the BMW Championship last week to stay in the mix for the FedEx Cup, and he secured it with a brilliant showing on Sunday.

Scheffler joins Rory McIlroy (3) and Tiger Woods (2) as the only golfers to win the FedEx Cup multiple times.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler captures another FedEx Cup and moves past Tiger Woods in PGA Tour career earnings
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler ended any conversation about who had the best season on Sunday when made up a three-shot deficit with a 4-under 66 to win the Tour Championship, claim a second FedEx Cup title and move past Tiger Woods for most PGA Tour career earnings.
articles.body: Scottie Scheffler ended any conversation about who had the best season on Sunday when he made up a three-shot deficit with a 4-under 66 to win the Tour Championship, claim a second FedEx Cup title and move past Tiger Woods for most PGA Tour career earnings. Scheffler signaled his rally with a 5-iron to within 2 inches of the cup on the 211-yard second hole. He caught Viktor Hovland with a 25-foot birdie on the fourth hole, pulled ahead for the first time on the 13th and held on to win at East Lake. “This was a week I brought a lot of good energy to the course and tried to do my best,” Scheffler said at the trophy presentation. “Coming from behind and being able to win tournaments is a really cool feeling.” Scheffler won for the third time this year — twice in the last three weeks during the PGA Tour’s postseason — to match Chris Gotterup, Matt Fitzpatrick and U.S. Open champion Wyndham Clark for most titles in 2026. He won his first FedEx Cup two years ago. Players vote on the Jack Nicklaus Award for PGA Tour player of the year. Scheffler has won the last four years — another would tie him with Woods for most consecutive awards. Taking over the top spot in career earnings was inevitable. The $40 million purse at the Tour Championship now counts as official money. Scheffler won $10 million, pushing his career total to $130,390,661. Woods, who never played for more than a $10 million purse during his peak years from 1997 through 2008, had been at the top of the career money list for nearly 26 years. It was a small slice of redemption for Scheffler, who lost in a playoff to Hovland at the Travelers Championship, one of his five runner-up finishes this year. Hovland made only one birdie and closed with a 72 to finish alone in second, worth $5 million. Scheffler had two bogeys — one a bad miss with a wedge from the fairway on No. 7, the other from a gnarly lie in the rough on the 14th — and still was the only player from the last three groups of the final round to break par. The final birdie came from a fairway bunker to 11 feet on the 16th. Hovland had three putts in a four-hole stretch catch the lip of the cup — two for birdie, one for par. Ryan Gerard, one shot behind Hovland staring out, made double bogey on the opening hole, followed with 13 straight pars and shot 72 to finish alone in third. Scheffler, who won his season opener in The American Express, ended the year with the 22nd title of his career — 13 of them by at least three shots — and 25th worldwide, including an Olympic gold medal in Paris two years ago.

articles.title: Tour Championship: Scottie Scheffler holds off Viktor Hovland to claim FedExCup title and break more PGA Tour records
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler claimed a second FedExCup title in three years; Scheffler posted a final-round 66 to hold off Viktor Hovland and Ryan Gerard, with Rory McIlroy finishing five strokes back in tied-fourth; Scheffler overtakes Tiger Woods in PGA Tour career money earnings
articles.body:
Scheffler overturned a three-shot deficit during an eventful Sunday at East Lake Golf Club, where he mixed six birdies with two bogeys to post a four-under 66 and pull clear of the field.

The world No 1 finished on 16 under and three strokes clear of Hovland, who led at various points on the final day, with Scheffler claiming the $10m first prize and joining Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods as the only multiple FedExCup champions.

Hovland posted a final-round 72 to finish second ahead of Ryan Gerard, with Rory McIlroy recovering from three bogeys in his first five holes to post a one-under 69 and share fourth spot.

McIlroy was joined on 11 under by Ludvig Åberg, Chris Gotterup, Russell Henley, Jacob Bridgeman, first-round leader Min Woo Lee and England's Alex Fitzpatrick, with defending champion Tommy Fleetwood a further shot behind.

Scheffler made an early statement by firing his tee-shot to tap-in range at the second, which lifted him within one when Hovland had to lay up from the rough at the first and opened with a bogey.

Overnight co-leader Gerard started with a double-bogey and never returned to the top of the leaderboard, as Scheffler drained a 24-foot birdie at the fourth to pull level with Hovland on 14 under.

Scheffler saved par from eight feet at the fifth but failed to take advantage of the par-five next, then cancelled out a poor approach into the seventh - resulting in a first bogey in 25 holes - by making a seven-foot birdie at the eighth.

Hovland fired a close-range birdie at the eighth to briefly reclaim the outright advantage on 15 under, only for Scheffler - playing two groups ahead - to start his back nine with a birdie and add another from five feet at the 13th to move ahead again.

The pair found themselves tied at the top when Scheffler missed the fairway off the 14th tee and made bogey, as Gotterup burned a 10-foot chance to get within one, but Hovland dropped a shot on the 13th to slip one behind with five to play.

Hovland produced a superb up and down from the 14th fairway to stay on 14 under, as Scheffler took control by recovering from finding a bunker off the 16th tee to make a 12-foot birdie and double his lead.

Scheffler two-putted the 17th and recovered from being forced to lay up to safely par the last, which was enough to close out a third PGA Tour win of the season and second of the FedExCup Playoffs.

His latest success sees him pass Woods in all-time career money earnings on the PGA Tour, while his 22 PGA Tour titles over the last five seasons is double any other player during that period.

The PGA Tour takes two weeks off before starting its FedExCup Fall schedule with the inaugural Biltmore Championship from September 17-20, held in Asheville, North Carolina.

articles.title: World number one Scheffler claims second Fedex Cup title
articles.summary: At times it felt like there was a certain inevitability about Scottie Scheffler collecting his second Fedex Cup title on Sunday.
articles.body:
16 S Scheffler (US); -13 V Hovland (Nor); -12 R Gerard (US); -11 A Fitzpatrick (Eng), C Gotterup (US), R McIlroy (NI), R Henley (US), MW Lee (Aus), J Bridgeman (US), L Aberg (Swe)

Selected others: -10 T Fleetwood (Eng), C Young (US), A Scott (Aus); -9 C Morikawa (US); -7 J Rose (Eng); -5 M Fitzpatrick (Eng), W Clark (US); E R MacIntyre (Sco)

At times it felt like there was a certain inevitability about Scottie Scheffler collecting his second Fedex Cup title on Sunday.

As those around him began to falter, the world number one, who started the day three strokes adrift of overnight leader Viktor Hovland, produced a typically metronomic performance with the winning cheque in sight.

And what a prize. Scheffler's reward for his 22nd career victory at the PGA Tour's season-ending Tour Championship in Atlanta will see his bank account credited to the tune of $10m (£7.4m).

The 2024 champion also joins Tiger Woods (2007 and 2009) and Rory McIlroy (2016, 2019 and 2022) to have won the event on multiple occasions.

"To come from behind and be able to win tournament is a really cool feeling," Scheffler said.

"There were a lot of talented guys in front of me on the leaderboard. I was fortunate to get off to a good start and put myself in the mix. It's a gift to be out here on tour. Each and every day I'm going to try to give it my best."

Across the final three pairings, Scheffler's four-under 66 was the only round to break par with his superb ability to find green after green giving him a substantial edge over his rivals.

Hovland, whose driving became more erratic, also found that his putter had gone cold when he most needed it, and the Norwegian signed for a two-over 72 as he finished three back in second place.

American debutant Ryan Gerard, who started one behind Hovland, ended the day in the same position and third overall on 12 under par after also taking 72 shots.

McIlroy was unable to rediscover the rhythm that rocketed him into contention on Saturday, with his topsy-turvy round of 69 containing four birdies and an eagle mixed with five bogeys.

Aside from the Northern Irishman there were few moments of sparkle on show elsewhere among the potential contenders, albeit Justin Rose's hole-in-one on the ninth was an obvious exception.

While Rose was unable to gather any momentum from that to seriously challenge, ending the day at seven under overall, another Englishman Alex Fitzpatrick matched Scheffler's 66, the lowest round of the day, to catapult himself up the leaderboard to conclude the tournament alongside six-time major winner McIlroy at 11 under.

It earned the 27-year-old a tie for fourth on his debut to cap a remarkable season in which he won his first DP World Tour event at the Indian Open before teaming up with his elder brother, the 2022 US Open champion Matt, to win the Zurich Classic of New Orleans pairs event.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler moves past a Tiger Woods money standard that stood for nearly 26 years
articles.summary: Tiger Woods was going for his seventh straight PGA Tour victory when he tied for second at Torrey Pines.  Scottie Scheffler won the Tour Championship to capt...
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Tiger Woods was going for his seventh straight PGA Tour victory when he tied for second at Torrey Pines. He earned $264,000 that day to move to No. 1 in career tour earnings.

That was Feb. 13, 2000, and Woods stayed there ever since — until Sunday.

Scottie Scheffler won the Tour Championship to capture his second FedEx Cup title and the $10 million prize — now considered official money — to raise his career total to $130,390,661.

Woods had been at $120,999,166 since he made his last cut on the PGA Tour at the 2024 Masters.

This is an entirely different era of golf, and Scheffler finally topping Woods in career earnings was inevitable. That it happened so quickly is a testament to Scheffler's dominance. He has been No. 1 in the world since May 2023.

The popularity and momentum Woods brought to the sport 30 years ago generated enormous spikes in prize money. And then with the arrival of Saudi-funded LIV Golf in 2022, the PGA Tour responded with even greater increases to keep more players from defecting.

There were 15 prize funds of $20 million or more this season on the PGA Tour schedule. Woods never played for a $10 million purse during his peak years from 1997 through 2009.

Woods won the FedEx Cup twice when it was worth $10 million, all in bonus money. Scheffler earned $23 million in bonus money last week by leading the FedEx Cup in points. The FedEx Cup finale has counted as official the last two years.

Most telling about the rapid increase in money was the 2024 Masters. Woods, at age 48 and trying to recover from multiple back surgeries and a 2023 car crash that shattered his right leg and ankle, finished in last place and made $44,000.

Scheffler won the Masters that year and moved to No. 12 on the career earnings list at $57,658,464. He has earned just over $72.7 million in his last 50 tournaments over two years and four months.

It was a matter of time, and it really doesn't matter to Scheffler.

"The reason our purses are so large today is because of the influence and impact that Tiger had on the game," Scheffler said before the Tour Championship started. "I wouldn't really consider that a Tiger record being broken. I think it just shows one of the many effects he had on the game of golf in a positive way."

Scheffler indicated last week in St. Louis the Tiger number he cares about his victories. Scheffler won for the 22nd time Sunday at East Lake. Woods shares the PGA Tour record at 82 victories.

articles.title: Cleveland Browns: 3 takeaways from the initial 53-man roster
articles.summary: The Browns announced their initial 53-man roster on Sunday. Here are three things that stood out about the group.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns joined their NFL brethren on Sunday in cutting their roster down to the initial 53-man squad ahead of the NFL-mandated deadline.

As everyone knows by now, the roster as it stands today is not the roster the Browns will take to Jacksonville in two weeks when they open the regular season against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Practice squads to be filled, waiver wires to be scoured for players, and a host of other roster manipulations will take place every week until the season comes to a close.

But it is the roster the Browns have for the moment, so here are three quick observations about the work that general manager Andrew Berry did today.

There was much hand-wringing and discussion about whether or not the Browns would and should keep four quarterbacks on the initial roster. (Let's set aside, for now, that it doesn't really matter how many they keep since none are worthy of being QB1.)

Berry ended up finding a way to keep all four – Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel, and Taylen Green – in the building for the moment, but that comes with a caveat.

While Watson, Sanders, and Green are on the roster, Gabriel will open the season on the injured reserve list with a back injury, meaning he will miss at least the first four games.

When did Gabriel come down with this injury? Who knows! The last time anyone saw him in action, he lit up the New England Patriots for 186 passing yards and three touchdowns in one half of action in Thursday's preseason finale.

The official word is that Gabriel hurt his back during the game and underwent an MRI on Saturday. So let's go with that for now.

In the end, it is a way for Berry to delay the decision about what to do with the quarterback room for a few more days or weeks. But it could be quite the risk if the Browns end up trading away a quarterback and Green is just one play away from seeing the field while Gabriel is unavailable.

All 10 members of the 2026 NFL Draft class made the initial roster, or at least survived being cut.

The only member not to be on the active roster is tight end Joe Royer, who was placed on the reserve/non-football illness list. Royer has not been with the team all summer, and no one is saying when he might return. But for now, he is still a member of the team.

As for the other nine selections, they all made the squad. Left tackle Spencer Fano, along with wide receivers KC Concepction and Denzel Boston, were always no-brainers. Safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren looks to be a key member of the secondary, while offensive lineman Austin Barber may find himself in the starting lineup sooner rather than later.

The rest of the class – center Parker Brailsford, linebacker Justin Jefferson, Green, and tight end Carsen Ryan – will all likely find a way onto the field at some point this fall.

In past years, that would be seen as a sign of weakness or because Berry needs to prove he is the "smartest guy in the room." But after the success of the 2025 draft class, it is another indication that the Browns may finally be on the right path.

The dream is temporarily over for the man from Kent State

It was always going to be hard for wide receiver Luke Floriea to find a roster spot, but that doesn't make the news that he was cut any easier.

Floriea was productive during the preseason, and everyone always likes a story of the local kid working his behind off when given the opportunity.

Hopefully this is not the last we see of Floriea, as a practice squad spot should have his name on it.

What do you say, Browns fans? Were you surprised by the initial roster? Happy? Frustrated? Let everyone know in the comments!

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler turns hot-mic F-bomb into motivation, rallies for Tour Championship win
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler erased a three-shot deficit to chase down Viktor Hovland at East Lake, but a controversial bunker ruling added drama to the finish.
articles.body: Scottie Scheffler shot a bogey-free 66 during Saturday’s third round at the Tour Championship and still looked frustrated throughout the round. After missing a putt at East Lake, Scheffler’s emotions finally boiled over and they were caught on a hot mic. "How does it go back that way? F---ing grain’s over here," Scheffler said. Scheffler’s inability to convert longer birdie looks in the third round left him three shots behind Viktor Hovland entering Sunday’s final round. But, as is often the case with the world’s best golfer, the minor struggles were covered up by stretches of incredible dominance. One day later, the putts started dropping and frustration turned into another Tour Championship trophy. SCOTTIE SCHEFFLER REVEALS HE PLAYED THROUGH 'PRETTY PAINFUL' ILLNESS DURING THE BMW CHAMPIONSHIP The world No. 1 came from behind on a punishing afternoon at East Lake, shooting a 4-under 66 to finish at 16-under and win the Tour Championship for the second time. Scheffler's Sunday 66 tied the low round of the day. No other player in the final three pairings shot better than 1 over. When Scheffler's tap-in par hit the bottom of the cup on the final hole, the tournament had effectively ended, even with four players still on the course. Scheffler chases down Hovland at East Lake It didn’t take long for Scheffler to let the entire field know that if they wanted to win the Tour Championship, they were going to have to outplay the top player on the planet. Scheffler nearly made an ace on the 211-yard par-3 second hole and easily tapped in for birdie. Meanwhile, Hovland made bogey on No. 1 and Ryan Gerard, who began Sunday one shot behind Hovland in the final pairing, doubled the opening hole. RORY MCILROY MAKES EMBARRASSING MISTAKE IN $10 MILLION TOURNAMENT, ANNOUNCER RIPS HIM FOR BEING TOO 'CUTE' Within minutes, Scheffler had turned a three-shot deficit into a one-shot deficit. Most people could probably figure out where this was heading next. Scheffler birdied Nos. 2, 4, 8, 10, 13 and 16, with bogeys at Nos. 7 and 14. His birdie at No. 13 gave him the outright lead for the first time in the tournament. The bogey at No. 14 briefly brought him back into a tie with Hovland, and Chris Gotterup had a birdie putt that would have moved him within one shot of the leaders. Gotterup missed it, nearly hit his tee shot into the water at the par-3 15th and made bogey after a poor chip. Another bogey at 16 ended his chances. That left the Tour Championship where it had felt headed for much of Sunday: Scheffler versus Hovland. Scheffler's birdie at No. 16 stretched the lead to two. Hovland had a chance to answer, but another birdie putt caught the lip and stayed out. The Norwegian dropped his putter in frustration, knowing that his chances of hoisting the trophy had all but ended. Hovland’s last real chance disappeared at No. 17, when he thinned his approach over the green and made another bogey. Hovland parred the final hole to close with a 2-over 72 and finish solo second at 13 under, three shots behind Scheffler. Gerard finished solo third at 12 under and one shot ahead of a seven-way tie for fourth that included Rory McIlroy. Hovland’s hot putter finally goes cold Hovland rode his putter to the Sunday lead. He made 141 feet, 3 inches of putts in the opening round, including seven from at least 10 feet, and closed Saturday’s 65 with six straight makes from at least seven feet. Sunday was the opposite. In the final round, Hovland’s longest made putt was a 6-foot par save. His 18-foot par putt at No. 13 lipped out after he appeared to think it was in and began walking after it. Birdie tries at Nos. 15 and 16 also caught the lip. Hovland’s driver didn’t help. He hit five of seven fairways on the front nine, then missed four straight on the back and five of seven over the final nine holes. JUSTIN ROSE SLAM DUNKS HOLE-IN-ONE DURING FINAL ROUND OF TOUR CHAMPIONSHIP ON EXTREMELY DIFFICULT PAR 3 His No. 13 bogey also brought the day’s biggest controversy. CBS showed an ultra-close replay that appeared to show Hovland’s club touch the sand as he began his backswing on a bunker shot. PGA Tour rules official Mark Dusbabek said the Tour received "several inquiries" about the shot but could not determine with certainty that the club made contact. No penalty was assessed. Under Rule 12.2b, touching sand with a club during the backswing for a shot from a bunker results in the general penalty of two strokes. The replays and still images appeared to show a mark in the sand behind Hovland’s ball, ensuring the decision will be debated despite Scheffler’s late separation. While it didn’t ultimately affect the winning score, it carried major payout implications. A two-stroke penalty would have moved Gerard into solo second and dropped Hovland into an eight-way tie for third at 11 under, which would have cost Hovland just over $3 million. Scheffler gets Travelers revenge and a defining 2026 win The victory also gave Scheffler revenge against Hovland after their earlier showdown at the Travelers Championship. Hovland’s only 2026 PGA Tour victory entering this week came at the Travelers, where he and Scheffler played together in Sunday’s final pairing before Hovland beat him in a Monday playoff. This time, Scheffler was not beside Hovland in the final group. He started three back, chased him down, and ultimately beat him by three shots. It was also a very different Tour Championship victory for Scheffler. His only previous Tour Championship win came in 2024, when he began at 10 under par due to the FedExCup Starting Strokes format. The PGA Tour eliminated starting strokes in 2025, putting every player at even par to begin this week. Scheffler’s 2024 win came with a built-in advantage. This one came after a three-shot deficit on Sunday. The title gives Scheffler three wins in 2026, along with 13 top-five finishes in 20 starts. He had already won The American Express and FedEx St. Jude Championship, while adding runner-up finishes at the Masters, RBC Heritage, Travelers Championship and 3M Open. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP He did not win a major this season, his first major-less year since 2023, but the Tour Championship gave Scheffler’s year a defining win and a strong case to win his fifth consecutive PGA Tour Player of the Year. Wyndham Clark is the main challenger after winning three times, including the U.S. Open and BMW Championship. But Scheffler’s ridiculous consistency, along with winning two FedEx Cup Playoff events in the past three weeks, makes it a tight race that could easily go either way. It was also a needed win for American golf. Europe won last year’s Ryder Cup, and non-Americans claimed three of the four majors this season. With the Presidents Cup next month, Scheffler delivered another reminder that the United States still has golf’s most reliable big-game player.

articles.summary: Any questions about whether Scottie Scheffler had loosened his grip atop the world of golf after he won just one regular-season event officially evaporated during the FedEx Cup playoffs.
articles.body:
Any questions about whether Scottie Scheffler had loosened his grip atop the world of golf after he won just one regular-season event officially evaporated during the FedEx Cup playoffs.

Scheffler won Sunday's Tour Championship, finishing 16-under to best Viktor Hovland by three strokes and securing his second playoff victory in three events. It was also his second FedEx Cup title in the past three seasons.

Here's a full look at the top finishers and their prize payouts:

Scheffler came into the final round three strokes back of Hovland but stormed back on Sunday. In many ways, it was reminiscent of a season where he perhaps wasn't at his best early on but finished in elite fashion.

"I think that's something I'm very proud of," he said of his playoff run. "I think when you look over the course of the season, and especially some of the tough starts, shooting over par to start a tournament on the PGA Tour is never a good spot to be in. I'm very proud of fighting back and having some good finishes and even giving myself some chances to win with some of those poor starts. Overall, [I] just continued to battle, day in and day out. It's something that I'm very proud of. It's a gift to be out here on tour. Each and every day, I'm going to try to give it my best."

Scheffler was never bad, of course, with five runner-up showings and 11 top-five finishes. Most golfers would kill for that type of season. But he reminded the world of golf that he has that next-level gear with Sunday's 4-under 66.

"Obviously, Scottie is unbelievable," Ludvig Åberg told reporters. "He's shown over and over again that he's world No. 1, and you can just look at the scores in the last couple of groups, and there were no real good scores except for that 66. I thought today was quite difficult, but he played solid golf. He takes control of the tournament."

To quote D'Angelo Barksdale, "the king stay the king." And Scheffler is very much the king in the modern era of golf.

articles.title: Community in 'harder position than immediately after synagogue attack - rabbi
articles.summary: Rabbi Daniel Walker says members of the Jewish community are feeling increasingly vulnerable.
articles.body:
The Jewish community at a synagogue where two men were killed in 2025 feels less safe now than it did immediately after the attack, its rabbi has said almost one year on.

Rabbi Daniel Walker said rising antisemitism, combined with a lack of action to "deal with core problems", had left many members of Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation in Manchester – and British Jews more widely – feeling increasingly vulnerable as the anniversary of the attack approaches.

"I think we're actually almost in a harder position than we were even immediately after the attack," he said ahead of a memorial service for the victims and survivors which will take place later today.

"I think the sense of vulnerability has grown. It hasn't diminished."

Two men, Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby, were killed and three others were injured as they tried to defend their synagogue from attacker Jihad al-Shamie on Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar, on 2 October 2025.

A wave of worldwide attacks followed over subsequent months.

In Sydney, Australia, 15 people were killed in a shooting at a celebration for the festival of Chanukah on Bondi Beach.

In London, Jewish people and property were targeted in arson attacks, including in March on ambulances belonging to the Hatzola emergency medical service .

In April, two orthodox Jewish men were stabbed as they left morning prayers in Golders Green.

A BBC Freedom of Information request to police forces in England and Wales has found that across 33 forces, violent hate crimes targeting Jewish people – such as harassment and assault – have risen by nearly two thirds since 2022.

For the Heaton Park congregation, Rabbi Walker said a "year of difficulty and of grief and of pain" had been made even harder by the attacks elsewhere.

"Something has gone seriously wrong in our society," he said.

"I think we're dealing with symptoms. We're extremely grateful for the increased security, but I don't think there's really any evidence of anyone dealing with the core problems.

"And on the contrary, in many ways, those may have become worse over the last months."

Angela Rayner told the BBC the government would "not allow hatred to drive people from their communities, to make them afraid to live and practise their faith freely or to divide our country".

"Antisemitism is a poison, and we won't stop fighting it until every Jewish person can live their lives fully, and free from fear," the cabinet minister for communities said.

A memorial service will take place at Heaton Park synagogue later to commemorate the victims and survivors.

Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis and Mayor of Manchester Bev Craig will be among those attending.

For those affected by the attack, the physical and emotional consequences are still being felt.

Bernard Agyemang, a security guard, is still recovering from the severe injuries he suffered when al-Shamie drove a car into him before trying to get into the synagogue with a knife.

Agyemang said he continued to struggle with the memories of the attack.

"The events of that day will stay with me forever," he said.

"I still live with the physical injuries and the emotional trauma caused by the attack, and there are days when the memories feel just as vivid as they did a year ago."

The 44-year-old from south Manchester suffered multiple fractures, including to his right leg and collarbone, as well as a suspected brain injury.

He continues to experience physical pain, cognitive difficulties and psychological trauma including PTSD.

Agyemang condemned the "hatred and violence that caused so much suffering" last year.

"Anniversaries like this are a reminder of everything that was taken from our community," he said. "But they are also an opportunity to come together, support one another and remember those we lost.

"My thoughts are with the families of Melvin and Adrian.

"No words can ease the pain of losing loved ones in such terrible circumstances."

Although the first anniversary of the Heaton Park attack isn't until October, the Jewish community will mark it on the religious anniversary date rather than by the secular calendar.

The attack happened on Yom Kippur, which falls in September this year. Private prayers will be held at the synagogue on that day.

Rabbi Walker said today's additional service is being held because the community also wanted to hold a public memorial before the Jewish High Holy Days – both to ensure those affected are remembered by wider society and to call for change.

"I think it will be a time when a lot of our community will be asking ourselves and the rest of society how we're going to make sure this doesn't happen again," he said.

"I don't think that's been done yet. I don't think the community feels secure enough yet, for good reason."

In a statement, the family of Melvin Cravitz thanked all those planning to attend the event and said that it "provides us with strength and support in recognising the utmost importance of remembering and honouring Melvin and Adrian and everyone impacted by the attack on Heaton Park synagogue and on our community on Yom Kippur last year."

There will be tight security at the commemoration, with a police operation on a similar scale to those deployed for football matches and music events in Manchester, the BBC has learned.

The chief constable of Greater Manchester Police, Sir Stephen Watson, is due to speak at the memorial event.

He apologised in July after it emerged that phones were twice seized from the attacker months before the car and knife assault but were not examined.

A force spokesperson said its increased resources would "provide additional visibility and security".

"These plans have been formed following engagement with community leaders to best understand local concerns and to ensure that the Jewish community that enjoy this special period without fear of harm," they said.

The BBC Freedom of Information request found that antisemitic criminal damage and arson offences have almost doubled since 2022.

In Manchester, there were 150 antisemitic hate crimes recorded by Greater Manchester Police in the first seven months of 2026 - only 32 fewer than in the whole of 2025.

articles.title: Tour Confidential: Scheffler wins, captain's picks, Good Good controversy
articles.summary: This week's Tour Confidential breaks down Scottie Scheffler's latest win, what Team USA should look like and the Good Good ad fallout.
articles.body:
Check in every week for the unfiltered opinions of our writers and editors as they break down the hottest topics in the sport, and join the conversation by tweeting us at @golf_com . This week, we discuss Scottie Scheffler's FedEx Cup win, captain's picks galore and the Good Good-Callaway fallout

Scottie Scheffler came from three strokes back after 54 holes to win the season-ending Tour Championship on Sunday at East Lake, claim the $10 million first-place check and pick up his third win of the season. Was this his best win of 2026? And did these last few weeks salvage his first major-less season in three years?

Sean Zak, senior writer: No, the best win of his season was two weeks ago… when he won by eight. I maintain stunned by how quickly we moved on from an 8-shot victory. If ANY other golfer on earth did that, we'd pause and talk about it for an entire week. I do think, in a way, this helps his major-free season feel a lot better. He was so good all year, but the pro golf world cares about dubs. He needed a couple dubs.

Josh Schrock, associate news editor ( @schrock_and_awe ): Agree with Sean. I thought the domination in Memphis was his best win of the season, especially with the chatter surrounding all his near-misses. I don't think it makes up for coming up short at the four tournaments that will define his legacy, but three wins sounds a lot better than one.

Josh Sens, senior writer ( @joshsens ): Agreed about Memphis being the bigger win. As for the season, the man had three top 5s in the majors and finished inside the top 15 in all of them. Jack Nicklaus and Tiger Woods both had multiple seasons without majors. Scheffler's so-called "disappointing" season is a fiction perpetuated by social media chatter and assorted golf outlets trying to perpetuate a story that isn't one.

Dylan Dethier, senior writer: Memphis was more dominant, sure — but East Lake had a real door-slamming quality to it thanks to its position on the schedule. Schaffer "only" won three times this year, but he won his first start and his last. Picked up a few extra bucks, too.

Who won the FedEx Cup Playoffs without winning the FedEx Cup Playoffs?

Zak: Good Q. I think the answer is Ryan Gerard, who is a helluva player and has his eyes set on a late charge into the American Presidents Cup team. I'm not sure he did enough to make the squad, but he did a lot of it in the last month or two. Brandt Snedeker would be wise to give him a long look.

Schrock: Gerard played great golf and will play on the DP World Tour next week as he looks to stay fresh in case he gets the P-Cup call. I'll go with Viktor Hovland, who had a chance to win the FedEx Cup despite still fighting his swing. He seems close to being back.

Sens: Good calls above. To add a third name to the list, how about the continued run of Matt Fitzpatrick's brother, Alex. A player on no fan's radar last year, now with good footing in the firmament. And another good finish this week.

Dethier: Wyndham Clark's BMW victory added another layer of legitimacy to an elite season. Scheffler dominated Clark in every season-long statistical category — but if we're just talking wins, there's no beating a U.S. Open, a playoff dub and three in all.

The Tour announced its new postseason format that will go into place come 2028, and it includes one 90-player, 72-hole stroke-play event named the "Championship Series Finale," with 32 players advancing to two weeks of match-play competition to name a "Tour Champion." Do you like it? An improvement?

Zak: I think it'll grade out as an 8 outta 10. Which is about three or four notches above where the current Tour playoffs sits. Anyone picking it apart is trying really hard to misunderstand commercial value, the share of golf attention across the governing bodies, and the desire among basically everyone for a serious match play event on the schedule. Now, the only real match play among individuals at the elite level of pro golf happens in August on the PGA Tour. That's a huge win.

Schrock: Massive win. The PGA Tour's postseason greatly needed a shakeup and I think having something that is easy for fans to understand and brings commercial appeal is much needed. Getting two weeks of match play at venues we don't normally see will be a massive boost for golf's postseason.

Sens: I think Sean is being a bit generous as to where the current playoffs sit. They're a cash grab and a snooze. Always have been. The new format is a huge improvement and not just because the bar for getting better was so low. Match play is a great format. Can't imagine a better change. Will it make the playoffs riveting? I'm skeptical. But it will make them miles better, for sure.

Dethier: The format change is fun — but I think the venue shift is, too. As is the potential reduction in outrageously sweaty golfers. We just spent August in Memphis, St. Louis and Atlanta, after all…

U.S. Presidents Cup captain Brandt Snedeker will finalize his team with six captain's picks he'll announce on Tuesday. If you are Sneds, who are you selecting? And who will be the biggest snub?

Zak: If I'm Snedeker, I'm taking the following as absolute LOCKS: Chris Gotterup, Xander Schauffele, Justin Thomas and Patrick Cantlay.

I'm feeling great taking Maverick McNealy as a team event rookie, but then comes the hard selection, ONE of the following: Jackson Koivun, Akshay Bhatia, Ben Griffin, J.J. Spaun and Ryan Gerard. I think Sneds goes Koivun, making Gerard the biggest snub. All the others haven't done enough lately.

Schrock: I would take Chris Gotterup, Xander Schauffele and Justin Thomas to start. Patrick Cantlay showed life in the playoffs but for me, it's not enough. I'd like to see the final three spots go to Jackson Koivun, Ryan Gerard and Maverick McNealy to give some guys who haven't played in team events some exposure before we start talking Ryder Cup.

Sens: The more fresh faces, the better. Along with Gotterup, give me McNealy, Gerard, Koivun, Griffin, and Spaun. We've seen plenty of the others. This is supposed to be an exhibition. Give us some new exhibits.

Dethier: Xander, Cantlay, Gotterup, Gerard, Thomas. The remaining spot is a complete wild card, especially after JJ Spaun's WD in East Lake. It'll let Snedeker show off his creative side, if he so chooses. Tie goes to the highest ceiling — gimme Koivun.

In other team-event news, U.S. Solheim Cup captain Angela Stanford rounded out her team with three captain's picks she made last week, although two of them (Rose Zhang and Megan Khang) have struggled lately but excelled in the Solheim Cup. Like the move? Or dislike it?

Schrock: I liked going with Rose, who finished T4 this week and is showing signs of life. I would've gone with Kiara Romero as my final pick and left Khang off. The U.S. hasn't won on away soil since 2015 so I'd roll the dice on the young budding star.

Zak: Khang has been a Solheim Cup killer in her career. No qualms with that pick. Zhang, on the other hand, is probably just a veteran play. She's been in a few of these now — even one on the road. The experience never hurts.

Sens: No quibbles with the Zhang pick and can get behind the Khang pick for personal reasons. I went to high school with her dad (makes me feel old), who was a killer in every sport he picked up and was especially merciless in one-on-one competitions. I see where his daughter gets it.

Dethier: Zhang made Stanford look smart (all sorts of unintended wordplay there) with a T4 this week, and Khang's T27 was her best result in months. Romero would have been fun, but the entire picks cycle was a reminder that this time around the U.S. bench isn't as deep as some years past. The biggest question going forward is what happens with Angel Yin, who was an auto-qualifier but has missed significant time with an illness and shot 81-76 in her first event back. So we may have one pick ahead still…?

Last week's news cycle was dominated by YouTube giants Good Good Golf and the fallout stemming from their controversial driver ad. Since the ad circulated they were dropped by Callaway Golf, had their merchandise removed from certain stores, are no longer partnering with the PGA Tour for a November event and had their "Big Break" show on Golf Channel canceled before it even aired. While we've already discussed this topic in great detail over the last week, what's your takeaway from it all? What did you learn?

Zak: My biggest takeaway was that it felt so very of this generation. A traditional brand going out of its way to use content creators/influencers to sell product. (We've seen a lot of that in this sport.) Good Good, made up of Gen Z'ers, are the company founders, its most recognizable faces and are, much like podcasters, right there in the advert selling an item. Then, the marketing team — which is catching all the late blame, it seems — is trying to spoof off a summer movie, as though it's a TikTok trend you just have to get in on. It all was extremely this era, this generation, etc., inclusive of the sequence of apologies that followed.

Schrock: I think Sean nailed it. As brands try to connect with and sell to a younger audience, they are going to have to decide how they can do so without letting the creators drive the car unchecked. It was a traditional brand trying to do a traditional ad with an untraditional marketing force in an attempt to reach an audience it covets. I'm interested to see how this dance evolves or if this is the start of a backlash where traditional big companies fall back on tried and true methods and decide not to venture into the creator lane.

Sens: Mostly, the whole thing just made me want to take up residence in a shack in the woods without an internet connection. If social media went away tomorrow, we'd lose some occasionally funny content but the world would be much better off. This week was a reminder of how these platforms bring out the worst in everyone. But no doubt Sean and Schrock are also right about the way it underscores the cultural/economic divides in golf and how the industry's efforts to "grow the game" have a way of blowing up into controversy.

Dethier: I yearn for a world where every event doesn't get jammed directly into the Great Culture War Machine. Unfortunately, here we are.

But, yeah. The ad was bad, the response was slow and underwhelming and by that point Good Good's brand damage had been done; the story had broken contain. When you have non-golfers on TikTok deep-diving Good Good's brand strategy, something has gone gravely wrong. Anyway, I'll be looking for space in the woods near Sens.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler overtakes Tiger Woods in PGA Tour career money list at Tour Championship to cap off dominant FedExCup season
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler completed another dominant PGA Tour season with Tour Championship victory and a second FedExCup title; Scheffler has now won 22 times on the PGA Tour since the start of 2022 and overtaken Tiger Woods on the PGA Tour career money list
articles.body:
While financial earnings between the two are difficult to compare, given the enormous spikes in prize money since Woods' prime era, it highlights just how dominant Scheffler has been on the PGA Tour to overtake the record so quickly.

Woods' total on the official PGA Tour career money list remains at $120,999,166, having last featured competitively in 2024, while Scheffler broke through the $130m barrier with his impressive Tour Championship victory at East Lake.

A three-shot win over Viktor Hovland saw Scheffler join Woods and Rory McIlroy as the only players with multiple FedExCup titles, with his latest success a third PGA Tour victory of another impressive campaign.

"To come from behind and be able to win the tournament is a really cool feeling," Scheffler said. "There was a lot of talented guys in front of me on the leaderboard. I was fortunate to get off to a good start and put myself in the mix."

Scheffler's Tour Championship triumph means he bookends his season with victories, having started his campaign by claiming The American Express before having a seven-month wait to next find the winner's circle.

He ended inside the top four 10 times during that frustrating winless period, with a runner-up finish to Rory McIlroy at The Masters among five seconds, although still entered the FedExCup Playoffs as No 1 for a fifth consecutive season.

Scheffler responded with a dominant eight-shot win at the FedEx St. Jude Championship, the opening FedExCup Playoff event, while his victory at East Lake sees him become just the 31st player to reach 22 career wins on the PGA Tour.

"I felt like my thought process going into (the FedExCup Playoffs) was that maybe I've underperformed in some of the post-seasons in the past," Scheffler said. "I think of 2022 and 2023, where I had a lead at this tournament and wasn't able to win the FedExCup or a Playoff event.

"I came in this year maybe not winning the tournaments that I could have won throughout the regular season, so to come in and win two out of three Playoff events is definitely a nice way to finish off the season."

It marks the fifth year in a row that Scheffler has won multiple PGA Tour titles, equalling Woods' career-best streak, while he becomes the first player since Dustin Johnson from 2016-18 to claim three or more victories in three consecutive seasons.

"Three wins, five runner-ups and finishing the season No 1 - those are some numbers to be proud of," Woods posted on X. "Incredible consistency all season long. Congrats on a historic season, Scottie."

How Scheffler's 'got an edge' over PGA Tour rivals

Scheffler's strokes-gained stats were nearly a shot a round better than his closest challenger over the PGA Tour season, plus he topped tee-to-green, greens in regulation and scoring average metrics during another super year.

"I think he [Scheffler] knows that he's got an edge on most guys out here." Hovland said. "He doesn't have to do anything crazy. He can play smart and just pick his spots, stay in it constantly.

"Today [Tour Championship], it wasn't like anybody else really played all that great in contention - a lot of guys were just gagging and throwing up. That's where he stays in it and shoots a nice score and that gets the job done."

Only Greg Norman and Woods have had more time as the world No 1 than Scheffler, who holds such a commanding lead over McIlroy and the chasing pack that - regardless of results over the rest of the year - he will start 2027 still in top spot.

Scheffler has been world No 1 since May 2023 but would need to stay there until October 2028 to break Woods' record consecutive stint of 281 weeks at the top, with the four-time major champion keen to keep building on his success.

"I feel like I hold myself to a high standard, which I think sometimes can be good and bad," Scheffler admitted. "I feel like at times I probably could be a bit of a pain to be around when things aren't going the way they should.

"I don't feel like I take days off. I'm highly competitive and I'm very proud of being able to have the consistent results I've had over the years. I feel like it's something that's very difficult to do.

"I don't take days off during tournaments. I try to give it my all each and every day. I feel like it's a gift to play out here on the PGA Tour and don't want to take it for granted.

"I don't want to look back at the end of my career and feel like I could have done more in order to play well. I want to be able to tell myself when I hang it up that I did everything I could. I feel like years like this show to myself how important that is."

When a 15-time major champion is using adjectives like 'incredible' and 'historic' to describe your season, you know you are doing something right. With every passing year, Scheffler keeps hitting generational standards not seen since Woods at his best.

The PGA Tour takes two weeks off before starting its FedExCup Fall schedule with the inaugural Biltmore Championship from September 17-20, held in Asheville, North Carolina.

Scheffler will feature for Team USA in the Presidents Cup a week later, when they host the International Team at Medinah and chase an 11th consecutive victory in the biennial contest. Get latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW .

articles.title: LIV Golf ofrece quitas a los jugadores y camina hacia el concurso de acreedores
articles.standfirst: Ha puesto sobre la mesa una propuesta para extinguir los contratos que no ha podido cumplir
articles.summary: Ha puesto sobre la mesa una propuesta para extinguir los contratos que no ha podido cumplir
articles.body: Acabado el curso de golf salvo en el DP World Tour, donde empieza la temporada alta, la atención se centra en la situación en la que van a quedar las distintas estructuras con la posible integración de nuevo en el PGA Tour de Jon Rahm y Bryson DeChambeau, si es que llegan a un acuerdo. La vencida aventura del LIV Golf, al menos el 1.0., después de que en abril el Fondo Público de Arabia (PIF) anunciara el cese del flujo económico a esta competición -5.600 millones de dólares desde su fundación en 2002-, tiene consecuencias inmediatas. A los golfistas, empezando por Rahm, el jugador al que más se le adeuda, le han ofrecido una primera propuesta: una quita para solventar los contratos que aún permanecen de una sensible rebaja. La oferta, avanzada por el 'Financial Times', obligará a un esfuerzo final al PIF que pondría 100 millones de dólares más para resolver estos contratos, al tiempo que es probable que LIV Golf se declare en bancarrota -el denominado Capítulo 11 en Estados Unidos- para reorganizarse y permita que la empresa siga operando mientras paga a acreedores según un plan aprobado por un tribunal. El panorama está rodeado de incertidumbre. A un despido masivo de empleados, se une las especulaciones sobre si con el apoyo del fondo BC Partners -dispuesto a entrar con 200 millones de dólares-, se podrá poner en marcha el LIV Golf 2.0., el circuito ideado para 2027 con 10 torneos y una sensible rebaja en los premios, nada parecido a los 30 millones por los que los 57 jugadores pugnaban esta temporada. El curso, cabe recordar, acabó abruptamente con la cancelación de la prueba de Nueva Orleans en junio y el final por equipos en Michigan. Las negociaciones están siendo individuales. Rahm y DeChambeau parecen tener un hueco abierto en el PGA Tour, pero el resto tendrá que buscarse la vida. Jóvenes como Michael La Sasso, ganador de la prueba de Indianápolis, Josele Ballester y Luis Masaveu ya se han inscrito en las fases de clasificación de la Escuela del DP World Tour para asegurarse un futuro para la próxima temporada.

articles.title: Women’s TGL: Five line-ups for inaugural season unveiled with Charley Hull and Lexi Thompson among big names
articles.summary: WTGL will take place at SoFi centre in Florida, the same venue which has hosted the men's competition since its inaugural season in 2025; England's Charley Hull and world No 2 Jeeno Thitikul are among the players to be named in the five founding teams
articles.body:
Created by golf icons Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy's TMRW Sports, who launched the men's TGL in 2025, alongside the LPGA at the start of the year, 25 players including Charley Hull and Jeeno Thitikul have been split into five teams of five.

The teams boast 48 combined Solheim Cup team appearances including eight selections for the 2026 competition and 15 major championships.

They also have a combined 28 Olympic appearances, representing 13 countries.

Atlanta Drive: Nataliya Guseva, Charley Hull, Andrea Lee, Minjee Lee and Yuka Saso

Boston Common Golf: Céline Boutier, Chizzy Iwai, Megan Khang, Lottie Woad and Ina Yoon

Los Angeles Golf Club: Aki Iwai, Alison Lee, Gaby Lopez, Kiara Romero and Michelle Wie West

Motor City Golf Club: Brooke M. Henderson, Jeeno Thitikul, Lexi Thompson, Ruoning "Ronni" Yin and Albane Valenzuela

New York Golf Club: Linn Grant, Danielle Kang, Lydia Ko, Yana Wilson and Rose Zhang

The league will be played at the purpose-built indoor venue the SoFi centre in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, with the men's league playing there since its inaugural season.

"WTGL will combine teams of world-class LPGA Tour stars with the energy of fans inside SoFi Center to create a thrilling new experience for women's golf," Rufus Hack, president of golf at TMRW Sports, said.

"The five teams will go head-to-head throughout November and December, creating a consistent spotlight for women's team golf and giving fans a new way to see the players' personalities, competitive instincts and decision-making as team-mates.

"With the rosters now set, the teams' identities and rivalries can begin to take shape."

The WTGL's five teams will compete in a round-robin regular season where every match carries postseason implications, building to the play-offs with single-elimination, semi-finals and a best-of-three finals, and is aligned with the LPGA Tour and offseason schedule.

articles.title: Rare footage and photos of Coventry on display at exhibition
articles.summary: Coventry Then & Now will feature archive photos, rare cathedral films and contemporary images.
articles.body:
An exhibition showing visual records of a city's past and present will bring together three collections for the first time.

Coventry Then & Now will feature archive photographs of the city, rare film footage of the construction of Coventry Cathedral and contemporary images.

The exhibition, which opens on 11 September, tells the story of more than 70 years of history.

Alan Denyer, head of LTB Showrooms, the volunteer-run community arts venue where the exhibition will be held, said: "When you walk round Coventry, you think you have seen it all, but a good photograph can see a new image, a new angle, and there is some really great stuff."

Among the exhibits will be 60 images by Elizabeth Tyler, a former Coventry College of Art student, who walked the streets of the city with a 1933 Rolleicord camera in the 1960s.

Earlier this year, she rediscovered the collection in her attic and has now made it available for the first time.

"When you come across new images, particularly of streets that aren't so famous, it is really special," Denyer said.

"I love the detail you get from Tyler's photos, from the fashion to the hairstyles to the way that the houses are decorated."

The second part of the exhibition features a rare public screening of the original colour 16mm films made by Coventry architect Barnard Reyner that document the complete construction of Coventry Cathedral, which began in 1956.

The films capture craftsmen at work, royal visits, the installation of major artworks, the raising of the cathedral spire and the consecration ceremony in May 1962.

Denyer said the films were "fascinating to see", as "this was someone observing something that was happening in front of them".

Jaguar Photographic Society was also involved in taking 60 images of present-day Coventry, which will be on display.

The exhibition will be in the Priory Undercrofts and run until Sunday 20 September.
