articles.title: Scottie Scheffler celebrates FedEx Cup title with a rare beer, offers warm praise for Brandel Chamblee
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler grabbed a rare cold beer after winning the Tour Championship and FedEx Cup, then gave Brandel Chamblee a memorable compliment.
articles.body: Scottie Scheffler was in a great mood on Sunday evening after winning the Tour Championship and wrapping up the FedEx Cup. After securing his third victory of the year and picking up a $10 million check in the process, he celebrated like most would, by enjoying a cold beer in the clubhouse before hitting the countless media stops on the property before leaving Atlanta. Scheffler also handed out a huge compliment to Golf Channel's Brandel Chamblee during his post-victory sit-down with the network. While it was a straightforward gesture, it showed a side of Scheffler we don't often see, which is a completely laid-back guy who was both ecstatic and relieved that he ended his 2026 campaign on top. To close out his post-round news conference in the media center, Scheffler was asked what sort of celebratory dinner he was going to get into. The World No. 1 explained that all he wanted was a cheeseburger, but he did let everyone know he enjoyed a nice cold beverage before sitting down to answer questions. THE SCOTTIE VS TIGER COMPARISON, MICHAEL BLOCK'S PARTY GETS SHUT DOWN, AND A FINAL WORD ON YOUTUBE GOLF DRAMA "I had a beer for the first time in a long time. It just sounded good," Scheffler explained. "Right when we got off the course, I got in there, these guys are trying to get me to do media and all this stuff. I was like: how much time do we really have? They're like we've got a couple minutes. All right, let me go inside and get some air conditioning. There was an open bar inside, and I'm like, all right, I'm grabbing a beer. It tasted great. "I don't really drink very often. My wife and my manager were like, wow, I haven't seen you have a beer in a long time. Well, season's over now. I'm going to have a beer. Well-earned beer." Yes, most would say the beer Scheffler sank after his round was well-earned, given his three-win, five-runner-up campaign that saw him earn $31 million before bonuses are added. SCOTTIE SCHEFFLER SHARES A PERFECTLY IMPERFECT ASSESSMENT OF WORK-LIFE BALANCE, THE CHALLENGES OF FATHERHOOD Scheffler then went on to join the Golf Channel's post-game show, and before leaving the set, he tipped his cap to Chamblee and the plethora of research and notes he puts together week in and week out. Chamblee, like any great broadcaster, has his fair share of supporters and critics, but there is no denying that he is a walking encyclopedia of golf knowledge. Whether it be golf history or the modern game, there may not be another human out there who has a brain filled with more knowledge about the sport. Scheffler giving props to Chamblee, and grabbing a page of his notes to show viewers back home made for a cool moment, and, again, presented a side of Scheffler that we don't get to see too often. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP There's nothing 'normal' about Scheffler on paper – this is a guy who has been the No. 1 ranked player in the world for 207 consecutive weeks – but at the end of the day, he's just someone who appreciates hard work and likes to hand out a compliment. At least with a beer in his system, that is.

articles.title: Rory McIlroy's 'desire' will dictate future as Scottie Scheffler tipped to relight opponent's 'fire'
articles.summary: Six-time major winner Rory McIIlroy made admissions over his enthusiasm for competing at the highest level at the FedEx Cup; The Sky Sports Golf Podcast discussed McIlroy's future and what he may need to motivate him to get back to being world No 1
articles.body:
The Northern Irishman finished in a seven-way tie for fourth at the FedEx Cup over the weekend, finishing five shots off tournament winner Scottie Scheffler despite showing earlier signs of promise.

Now 37, six-time major winner McIlroy admitted his "fuse was shorter than it used to be" before the final round at the East Lake Golf Club.

He had arrived in Atlanta off the back of three weeks of competing in a row, something he admitted he would never exceed again despite still managing a fourth-place finish over the weekend.

"That just tells you how good he is," Lee told the Sky Sports Golf Podcast . "But I think Rory's body language this week wasn't great. He looked slightly… is grumpy the right word?

"But he's just slightly off that kind of affable, bouncy Rory that we normally see. So there's stuff going on with him… Rory's in this position. He's played golf for 20 years at the highest level. He's 37.

"He realises there are other things in life, but the last thing he wants to do is not be able to be peak Rory. So his conundrum is 'how much can I pare back my schedule, but still perform the way I know I can?' That's the place he's in now.

"37 is still golfing prime. It's going to come down, for him, to desire. How much does he still want it? And if he still wants it, I think he's going to have to play a bit more."

McIlroy took an extended break after The Open, spending more time with his family before returning for this three-week run of events.

"I absolutely think he can win more majors," Lee continued. "But going along with that is you sacrifice your home life. You're not as home as much as you want to be… I actually think Rory is in mentally quite a good place at the moment, and he is focused on some family stuff at the moment."

Speaking before his final round, McIlroy admitted: "once you lose your enthusiasm to go to the course, it is time to take a break." That comment could suggest golf fans could be seeing less and less of the world No 2 as time goes on.

"I think that's plausible," Sean Zak agreed. "I think that the changes coming to the PGA Tour schedule could pull a little bit more out of him, could help him balance being a dual member a little bit better."

Zak went on to suggest McIlroy may need to set himself a goal of beating Scheffler to top spot to reignite his motivation.

"You know, of all the golfers at the top of the game, I think he better than most shows what things matter to him and shows the goals that he's set," he said.

"And I think ever since that Grand Slam-finishing Masters win, he has just struggled to really place "OK, what's the next goal?"

"When you look at 2025, when he won that Masters, the next goal was really, 'OK, let's win at Bethpage' - and then they did that.

"Then after that, it was 'gosh, OK, what is the next goal?' I think for him to live up to what we're asking him to do right now, what a lot of fans would like him to do, is his next goal needs to be taking Scottie off the top mark or matching Scottie in some way.

"I bet if Scottie won a major this year, Rory might feel a little bit more of the fire beneath him because you get to some point where they've all won a bunch.

"What is the tiebreaker? How many majors did you win? Rory still has a nice little lead on Scottie - but how long will that last? We think that he probably won't hold that lead.

"It's just funny because I think Rory McIlroy, let's say [at] 21 years old was like "I want to be number one in the world. I want to win every single tournament."

"Rory McIlroy, 37-year-old, he may have to do the same thing. It should be 'I want to be number one. I want the world to think I'm the best golfer because at my best, I certainly am.'"

McIlroy will next compete at the Irish Open, starting on September 10.

articles.title: Most PGA Tour players are taking a break, but Ryan Gerard took a red-eye to Switzerland
articles.summary: After finishing third in the Tour Championship, Ryan Gerard gathered his things and headed to the airport to catch a flight to Europe.
articles.body:
Ryan Gerard made a run at the FedEx Cup title. Then he made a run to the airport.

Some guys just love playing golf, and Gerard is one of them. After finishing third in the Tour Championship , he gathered his things and headed to the airport to catch an overnight flight to Europe.

"Well, I need to play two more DP World Tour events to maintain not being suspended from their Tour," he said. "So that was one of them."

He went on to add that perhaps this overseas excursion could benefit him should he be chosen as one of the six captain's picks for the Presidents Cup .

"Full transparency, if I get a Presidents Cup spot, I'd love to kind of roll into there being a little bit more prepared," he said. "I like to play a lot of golf. And if I don't, I'll probably just stay over there and play Wentworth and the France Open after that."

See the best photos from the 2026 Tour Championship at East Lake in Atlanta

Gerard is currently not in the projected top 15 , but maybe his performance at East Lake has him on captain Brandt Snedeker's radar.

"A bit of a weird stretch of the year for me. I like playing lots of golf. I feel like I'm at my most prepared when I'm in kind of a rhythm," Gerard said. "I'll be ready for whatever the future holds, but I need to get a couple more events in."

Todd Kelly is an assistant managing editor at Golfweek.
